name: limit-zstd-window-over-cap
description: A hand-built zstd frame declaring a 128 MiB window (windowLog 27) is refused before its content is expanded.

error.detail: declared window size exceeds the decoder's bound

grounding: The output cap alone bounds the bomb only after the bomb exists. The window bound refuses a hostile frame up front, at a cost of fourteen bytes read.

contested.question: Go bounds the zstd decoder with both WithDecoderMaxWindow and WithDecoderMaxMemory; the Rust binding exposes window_log_max only. What does the corpus assert?
contested.decision: The window bound, because it is the part that is observable from outside the decoder — this fourteen-byte frame distinguishes a decoder that sets it from one that does not. Max-memory is asserted nowhere: with the window already bounded at the output cap it changes no outcome this corpus can construct, so a case for it would be asserting one language binding's API surface rather than the capture policy.
contested.open: If a future frame shape is found that Go refuses on memory and Rust accepts, it belongs here as a new case and the divergence becomes real. Until then the two implementations are conformant with each other.
contested.asserted: window bound at windowLog 25 (= log2 of the 32 MiB output cap), inclusive

notes: Same frame as limit-zstd-window-at-cap with the window descriptor changed from 0x78 to 0x88 (exponent 17 -> windowLog 27). Nothing else differs, so the outcome difference is attributable to the window alone.
